title: Headaches: patterns, treatment and warning signs
intro: Headache is a symptom with many causes. Tension-type headache and migraine are common primary headache disorders; infection, injury or other illness can cause secondary headache. The pattern and accompanying features guide care.

sections.heading: Understanding the problem
paragraphs: Note whether pain presses or throbs, its location, duration, triggers and effects on activity. Nausea, light sensitivity or visual changes can matter; no single feature confirms migraine for everyone.

sections.heading: Assessment and tests
paragraphs: A headache diary should include headache days and all pain medicines used. Examination guides whether investigations are needed; routine scans are not required for every familiar stable headache pattern. Bring your medicine list and previous results; ask which findings would change the plan.

sections.heading: Treatment choices
paragraphs: Treatment differs by diagnosis. Simple analgesics may help occasional attacks, while migraine-specific or preventive treatment may be appropriate for others. Frequent pain-medicine use can itself sustain headache; discuss a supervised plan rather than escalating doses. Agree how benefit and adverse effects will be checked before changing treatment.

sections.heading: Everyday care
paragraphs: Regular meals, hydration, sleep and manageable activity can support care. Avoid blaming yourself for every attack or imposing broad restrictions from a generic trigger list. Work and school adjustments may reduce disability. Choose a routine you can maintain, and discuss barriers such as cost, work or language.

sections.heading: Follow-up and warning signs
paragraphs: Sudden maximal severe headache, new weakness, confusion, fever with stiff neck, vision loss or headache after significant injury requires urgent assessment. New severe headache during pregnancy or after birth also needs prompt care.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira records headache days and painkiller use. Review reveals increasing medicine use, prompting a planned treatment change rather than stronger daily tablets.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben’s familiar headache suddenly becomes very severe with arm weakness. He seeks emergency help rather than treating it as another routine attack.
